regexCodeList.string: ^Global Quest: Global Quest # \d+ has been won by \w+ - \d+(?:th|st|rd) win\.$

Script.name: chat
Script.script:
--[[ Chat — the channels in tabs, in a window you can move Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02 Eight tabs: All, Private, Group, Tell, Say, Spouse, Clan, Friend. The routing is the stock module's, because it's right and there is nothing to improve about it: tell -> Tell say -> Say gtell -> Group ftalk -> Friend clantalk -> Clan spouse -> Spouse anything else -> All only Those six also copy into Private, which is the point of that tab: everything addressed to you personally, in one place, without the channel noise. And everything lands in All. Off GMCP - comm.channel carries { chan, msg, player } with the MUD's own colours in the message - rather than off screen triggers. A trigger has to match text that moves with your settings; the channel name in GMCP does not. NOTHING IS GAGGED. The MUD's text stays in the main window exactly as it arrived; these are copies. That has been the rule since the search and shop windows and it holds here: additive, never a move. Each tab is its own MiniConsole rather than one console repainted on switching. Mudlet then owns the scrollback and the colours per tab, which is the whole job, and switching is a show and a hide. ]] aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.chat = aardkit.chat or {} local CH = aardkit.chat local U = aardkit.util.named("Chat") local CFG = U.load("chat", { on = true, active = "All", -- A tab that isn't the one you're looking at goes red until you look. Their -- module blinks; a steady colour says the same thing without moving. mark = true, fontSize = 9, -- ON, like the mapper's. Installing this takes the channels over: the stock -- module's onChannel stands down and its eight tabs come out of the frame, -- because two sets of chat tabs is worse than either. -- -- A switch, not a one-way door: 'chat standalone off' gives them back. -- Nothing of theirs is deleted, only disabled. standalone = true, }) local function save() U.save("chat", CFG) end --- -- the tabs -- -- Order is theirs, which is the order they read in: everything, then the -- personal aggregate, then the individual channels. --- local TABS = { "All", "Private", "Group", "Tell", "Say", "Spouse", "Clan", "Friend" } -- gmcp comm.channel 'chan' -> tab. Anything not in here goes to All alone, -- which is what the MUD's own channels (gossip, market, auction) do. local ROUTE = { tell = "Tell", say = "Say", gtell = "Group", ftalk = "Friend", clantalk = "Clan", spouse = "Spouse", } -- The six above are personal, so they copy into Private as well. local PRIVATE = { Tell = true, Say = true, Group = true, Friend = true, Clan = true, Spouse = true, } local TABH = 18 -- tab strip height -- Theirs. Same eight names as ours, which is no accident - we route the same -- channels the same way - but they're their windows in their frame, added by -- guiLoad with addWindow(All,"All","bottomright"). Removing them from the frame -- hides them; the objects stay alive because they aren't ours to destroy, and a -- reinstall of theirs just gets removed again next load. local THEIRS = { { "onChannel", "script", "routes comm.channel into its own eight tabs", "this module, from the same GMCP and the same routing" }, } -- Declared before anything that reads them. A table read by a function defined -- above it binds a nil global instead, which this project has paid for eight -- times over. local cons, tabs, unread, back = {}, {}, {}, nil --- -- the panel --- local panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "chat", title = "Chat", -- Bottom right, which is where the stock module put its tabs - so somebody -- coming across finds chat where their eye already goes. Dead centre of the -- screen, over the room descriptions, is where it started and that was -- wrong. Drag it anywhere; it remembers, like every panel here, and -- 'chat dock' pops it into a window of its own. x = "1050px", y = "530px", width = 560, height = 240, consoleless = true, -- eight of our own, one per tab onbuild = function() cons, tabs, back = {}, {}, nil if aardkit.chat and aardkit.chat.paint then aardkit.chat.paint() end end, -- paint, not layout. A resize can also be a dock or embed switch, and -- _build hands back a brand-new container - laying out against widgets -- that live in the old one puts them somewhere nobody can see. S&D learned -- this the same way. onresize = function() if aardkit.chat and aardkit.chat.paint then aardkit.chat.paint() end end, }) CH.panel = panel local function style(name) local on = (name == CFG.active) local hot = unread[name] and CFG.mark local fg = on and "#c8d0dc" or (hot and "#e94560" or "#8a93a8") local bg = on and "#1f2937" or "#0d1117" return "background-color: " .. bg .. "; border: 1px solid #3a4a6b;" .. " qproperty-alignment: 'AlignCenter'; color: " .. fg .. ";" end local function label(name) return "
" .. name .. (unread[name] and CFG.mark and " *" or "") .. "
" end function CH.restyle() for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do local b = tabs[name] if b then pcall(function() b:setStyleSheet(style(name)) end) pcall(function() b:echo(label(name)) end) end end end -- A container built this instant reports no size yet, and laying out against -- zero leaves eight consoles ten pixels wide - which looks exactly like an -- empty window you can see the game through, because that is what it is. -- So a layout that finds nothing to measure asks again shortly. local relayout = 0 function CH.layout() if not panel.container then return end local w = U.px(panel.container.get_width and panel.container:get_width() or panel.container.width) local h = U.px(panel.container.get_height and panel.container:get_height() or panel.container.height) if w < 40 or h < 40 then if relayout < 8 then relayout = relayout + 1 tempTimer(0.5, function() CH.layout() end) end return end relayout = 0 local each = math.floor(w / #TABS) for i, name in ipairs(TABS) do local b = tabs[name] if b then -- the last one takes the rounding, so the strip meets the edge local bw = (i == #TABS) and (w - each * (#TABS - 1)) or each pcall(function() b:move(each * (i - 1), 0) end) pcall(function() b:resize(bw, TABH) end) end end for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do local c = cons[name] if c then pcall(function() c:move(0, TABH) end) pcall(function() c:resize(w, h - TABH) end) end end if back then pcall(function() back:move(0, 0) end) pcall(function() back:resize(w, h) end) pcall(function() back:lower() end) end end -- Errors from the constructors are REPORTED, not swallowed. The window came up -- empty with a healthy 500x210 container and eight widgets that had never been -- built, and a pcall that throws its message away is why that took a round trip -- to explain: 'chat' could say nothing was built but not a word about why. local said_why = false local function build(what, fn) local ok, obj = pcall(fn) if ok and obj then return obj end if not said_why then said_why = true U.err("Couldn't build " .. what .. ": " .. tostring(obj)) end return nil end function CH.paint() if not panel.container then return end local gen = panel.gen or 1 if not back then local b = build("the backdrop", function() return Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_chat_bg_" .. gen, x = 0, y = 0, width = "100%", height = "100%", }, panel.container) end) if b then back = b -- solid, and behind everything: the container's own background is -- painted on the frame rather than the inside, so without this the -- main window shows through the gaps pcall(function() b:setStyleSheet("background-color: #0d1117;") end) pcall(function() b:lower() end) end end for i, name in ipairs(TABS) do if not tabs[name] then local b = build("tab " .. name, function() return Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_chat_tab_" .. name .. "_" .. gen, x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = TABH, }, panel.container) end) if b then tabs[name] = b -- a function, not a string: no quoting a tab name into Lua pcall(function() b:setClickCallback(function() CH.show(name) end) end) end end if not cons[name] then local c = build("console " .. name, function() return Geyser.MiniConsole:new({ name = "aardkit_chat_" .. name .. "_" .. gen, x = 0, y = TABH, width = 10, height = 10, autoWrap = true, scrollBar = true, fontSize = CFG.fontSize or 9, }, panel.container) end) if c then cons[name] = c pcall(function() c:setColor("#0d1117") end) end end end CH.layout() CH.restyle() for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do local c = cons[name] if c then if name == CFG.active then pcall(function() c:show() end) else pcall(function() c:hide() end) end end end end function CH.show(name) if not cons[name] then return end CFG.active = name unread[name] = nil save() for _, n in ipairs(TABS) do local c = cons[n] if c then if n == name then pcall(function() c:show() end) else pcall(function() c:hide() end) end end end CH.restyle() panel:raise() end -- What it thinks it has. When the window comes up empty this is the difference -- between guessing and knowing: a container with no size is one fault, eight -- consoles that were never built is another, and they look identical. function CH.diag() local w, h = 0, 0 if panel.container then w = U.px(panel.container.get_width and panel.container:get_width() or 0) h = U.px(panel.container.get_height and panel.container:get_height() or 0) end local nt, nc = 0, 0 for _ in pairs(tabs) do nt = nt + 1 end for _ in pairs(cons) do nc = nc + 1 end return w, h, nt, nc end --- -- what arrives --- -- The MUD's own colours. comm.channel carries ANSI, and ansi2decho is Mudlet's -- own converter for exactly this - which is what the stock module uses too. local function to_screen(msg) msg = tostring(msg or "") if U.has("ansi2decho") then local ok, out = pcall(ansi2decho, msg) if ok and out then return out end end return msg end local function put(name, text) local c = cons[name] if not c then return end pcall(function() decho(c.name, text .. "\n") end) if name ~= CFG.active then unread[name] = true end end --- -- the three the MUD prints but doesn't send -- -- comm.channel carries 51 channels, which is everything that IS a channel. -- These three aren't: they're screen text, and without them the tabs are -- missing things the stock module's tabs had. -- -- Remort Auction -> Private, All, Group -- Global Quest won -> All -- remote socials -> Private, All, Group -- -- Their list, their destinations. Copied off the screen with selectCurrentLine -- and appendBuffer, so the MUD's own colours come across intact and nothing is -- reconstructed - the same way the ASCII map capture works. --- local function copy_line(...) if not CFG.on then return end local where = { ... } pcall(selectCurrentLine) pcall(copy) for _, name in ipairs(where) do local c = cons[name] if c then pcall(appendBuffer, c.name) if name ~= CFG.active then unread[name] = true end end end CH.restyle() end function CH.capture(...) copy_line(...) end -- '^\*.*$' matches a great deal that is not a social, so the colour is what -- tells them apart: Aardwolf prints a remote social in teal. That test is -- theirs and it earns its place - without it this copies every line beginning -- with an asterisk into three tabs. function CH.capture_social() if not U.has("getFgColor") then return end pcall(selectCurrentLine) local ok, r, g, b = pcall(getFgColor) if not (ok and r == 0 and g == 128 and b == 128) then return end copy_line("Private", "All", "Group") end function CH.on_channel() if not CFG.on then return end local d = gmcp and gmcp.comm and gmcp.comm.channel if not (d and d.msg) then return end local tab = ROUTE[tostring(d.chan or ""):lower()] local text = to_screen(d.msg) if tab then put(tab, text) if PRIVATE[tab] then put("Private", text) end end put("All", text) CH.restyle() end --- -- commands --- local stood_down, unframed = false, false local function stand_down() if not CFG.standalone or not aard then return end if not stood_down then for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do aardkit.stock.cmd("off " .. t[1]) end stood_down = true end if not unframed and CH.unframe_theirs() then unframed = true U.note("Stock chat tabs taken out of the frame - two sets of tabs is worse" .. " than either. 'chat standalone off' hands them back.") end end function CH.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) -- 'x opacity 200' where somebody looks for it, rather than only -- 'panel x opacity 200'. One line; core does the work. if aardkit.panel.verb("chat", verb, rest) then return end rest = U.trim(rest) -- a bare tab name switches to it: 'chat clan' reads better than 'chat tab clan' for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do if verb == name:lower() then CH.show(name); return end end if verb == "repaint" then cons, tabs, back, said_why = {}, {}, nil, false CH.paint() local w, h, nt, nc = CH.diag() U.ok("Rebuilt: " .. nt .. " tab(s), " .. nc .. " console(s), container " .. w .. "x" .. h .. ".") return end if verb == "" or verb == "help" then local w, h, nt, nc = CH.diag() U.help("Chat", { { "state", CFG.on and "on" or "off" }, { "showing", CFG.active }, { "built", nt .. " tab(s), " .. nc .. " console(s), container " .. w .. "x" .. h .. (w < 40 and " <- no size, nothing can be laid out" or "") }, { "tabs", table.concat(TABS, " ") }, { "" }, { "chat ", "switch - 'chat clan', 'chat tell'" }, { "chat on|off", "stop collecting altogether" }, { "chat clear [tab]", "empty one, or the one you're looking at" }, { "chat mark on|off", "colour a tab that has something new" }, { "chat show|hide|dock|embed", "where the window lives" }, { "chat opacity <0-255>", "how solid this window is; 'default' to follow the shared setting" }, { "chat standalone on|off", "stop the stock module's own tabs" }, { "chat repaint", "rebuild the tabs and consoles from scratch" }, { "" }, { "Nothing is gagged - the MUD's own lines stay in the main window." }, { "These are copies, routed the same way the stock module routes them." }, }) elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on"); save() U.ok("Chat collection " .. verb .. ".") elseif verb == "standalone" then local v = U.trim(rest):lower() if v ~= "on" and v ~= "off" then local rows = { { "state", CFG.standalone and "on - ours has the channels" or "off - theirs is running too" } } if not aard then rows[#rows + 1] = { "installed", "no stock module - nothing to stand down" } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do rows[#rows + 1] = { t[1] .. " (" .. t[2] .. ")", t[3] } rows[#rows + 1] = { "", "-> " .. t[4] } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "", "-> and its eight tabs come out of the frame" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "chat standalone on|off", "switch it" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Nothing of theirs is deleted, only disabled." } U.help("Standalone chat", rows) return end CFG.standalone = (v == "on"); save() if not aard then U.note("The stock module isn't installed - ours already has the channels.") return end for _, t in ipairs(THEIRS) do aardkit.stock.cmd((v == "on" and "off " or "on ") .. t[1]) end if v == "on" then stood_down, unframed = false, false stand_down() U.ok("Stock chat off - ours has the channels.") else CH.reframe_theirs() stood_down, unframed = false, false U.ok("Stock chat back in its frame. Reload to be sure it's routing again.") end elseif verb == "mark" then CFG.mark = U.trim(rest):lower() ~= "off"; save() CH.restyle() U.ok("New-message marking: " .. (CFG.mark and "on" or "off")) elseif verb == "clear" then local which = rest ~= "" and rest or CFG.active for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do if name:lower() == which:lower() then local c = cons[name] if c then pcall(function() c:clear() end) end U.ok("Cleared " .. name .. ".") return end end U.warn("No tab called '" .. which .. "'. " .. table.concat(TABS, " ")) elseif verb == "show" or verb == "hide" or verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" then aardkit.panel.cmd("chat " .. verb) CH.paint() else U.warn("chat | on | off | clear | mark | show|hide|dock|embed ('chat help')") end end --- -- standing theirs down -- -- guiLoad builds its tabs on a timer after this script has run, so a single -- attempt at load is too early. It retries, and only says anything the first -- time it works. --- function CH.unframe_theirs() if not (GUIframe and GUIframe.removeWindow and GUIframe.initialized) then return false end local gone = false for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do if pcall(GUIframe.removeWindow, name, "bottomright") then gone = true end end return gone end function CH.reframe_theirs() if not (GUIframe and GUIframe.addWindow and GUIframe.initialized) then return false end local back = false for _, name in ipairs(TABS) do local w = _G[name] if type(w) == "table" then if pcall(GUIframe.addWindow, w, name, "bottomright") then back = true end pcall(function() w:show() end) end end return back end aardkit.register("chat", "the channels in tabs, in a window you can move", CH.cmd) aardkit.gmcp.need("chat", "Comm 1") aardkit.gmcp.watch("chat", "comm.channel", "aardkit.chat.on_channel", true) CH.paint() -- Their tabs, stood down. After the load AND after a connect: guiLoad builds -- them when the session connects rather than when this script loads, so a -- profile that opens disconnected has nothing to remove when the load timers -- fire - every one of them passes before their tabs exist. for _, t in ipairs({ 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 }) do tempTimer(t, stand_down) end U.killhandler(aardkit_chat_connect) aardkit_chat_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() for _, t in ipairs({ 2, 6, 12, 20 }) do tempTimer(t, stand_down) end end)
